commands.description: Runs an analysis on the latest result of a physics: polarization, capacitance_matrix, inductance_matrix, epr, hamiltonian, tls_participation, network, piezo_resonator, uq_cqed, far_field, beam_overlap, or optomechanics. For `capacitance_matrix`, optional `params` perform ground projection or floating Schur elimination (`ground`, `eliminate: "drop" | "floating_schur"`), grounded/differential lumped qubit reduction (`qubits: [{ name, pads, E_J_Hz? }]`), resonator ZPF / dispersive coupling extraction (`resonators: [{ name, terminal, f_r_Hz, Z0_ohm?, resonator_type?, C_r_F? }]`), and matched-asymptotic finite-metal-thickness correction (`metal_thickness_m`, `edge_cutoff_m`). For `hamiltonian`, outputs include `f_cav_Hz`, `g_matrix_Hz`, `kappa_cav_Hz`, and `t1_purcell_s`, and `params` accept `sweep_port` (0-based index or port name), `squid_asymmetry`, `squid_flux_sweep`, and `ej_hz_sweep`. For `tls_participation`, interface thicknesses/permittivities/loss tangents auto-load from the material TOML `[interfaces.{ma,ms,sa}]`, `params` accept `trench_depth_m` (substrate over-etch depth in metres), and passing `electrostatic_physics` (e.g. `"dfs"`, with optional `port_terminals`, `modal_voltages`, `modal_freqs_hz`) evaluates hybrid quasi-electrostatic modal TLS participation and `T1_TLS_s` on the fine electrostatic mesh. For `network`, extracts damped companion-QEP modes, ROM-synthesized Z/Y/S matrices, Schur-complement Black-Box Quantization (`bbq_modes`), Taubin algebraic circle-fit resonator parameters (`s21_fit`), and Touchstone v1.1 (`.sNp`) text from either `CircuitRom` or `DrivenPortData`. For `piezo_resonator`, extracts series/parallel resonance frequencies (`f_s_Hz`, `f_p_Hz`), IEEE coupling factors (`k_t2`, `k_eff2`), unwrapped phase-slope quality factors (`Q_s`, `Q_p`), and bounded 6-parameter mBVD equivalent circuit (`C_0`, `R_0`, `R_s`, `C_m`, `L_m`, `R_m`) from `DrivenPortData`. For `uq_cqed`, propagates fabrication and constitutive 1-sigma `uncertainties` (plus `seed`, `n_samples`, `electrostatic_physics` companion bounds) through zero-solve EPR/Hamiltonian/Capacitance/TLS post-processing while keeping ASME V&V 20 epistemic brackets strictly separated from aleatoric variances. For `optomechanics`, evaluates photoelastic (`g_pe_hz`), moving-boundary (`g_mb_hz`), total vacuum optomechanical coupling (`g_0_hz`, `m_eff_kg`, `x_zpf_m`), and stimulated Brillouin scattering gain (`sbs_gain_w_inv_m_inv`) across shared or independent optical (`optical_physics`) and mechanical (`mechanical_physics`) meshes (ADR 141). The reply carries `stale`, `age_s`, and `validated` of the result it was run on.

commands.description: Solves the physics on 1 comparison mesh (2-grid default) or 2 comparison meshes (3-grid Roache GCI when `grids: 3`) with element sizes scaled by `factor` (`< 1` refines, `> 1` coarsens, or inverted coarsening ladder `[1.0, 1/factor, (1/factor)^2]` when `coarsen: true`; the active project is never mutated) and compares every eigenvalue, value and scalar across grids. By default `scale_sizes` is true so non-suppressed `add_size` rules (`h`, `max_deviation`, `min_layers`) and `gap_cells` scale proportionally on comparison copies. Sub-solves are isolated through `nyx-worker` and admitted against machine RAM when available. When mode ordering changes between meshes, `match: "nearest"` pairs mutual nearest eigenvalues and `track` filters candidate modes by target (`f`, `n_b` or `n_eff`) and/or physical mode signatures. With `extrapolate` (`"richardson_log_spd"` or `"richardson_linear"`), computes Richardson extrapolation (`extrapolate_order` defaults to 1.0 on 3D/sheet capacitance matrices, else `2 * order`) and promotes extrapolated capacitance matrices when `apply_extrapolated` is true (tagging `SpatialErrorEstimate.extrapolated_scalars_only = true`).

commands.name: integrate
commands.summary: Integrate an expression over a region
commands.description: The integral of an expression of fields over a region (a region name, comma list or `name*`; default the whole mesh), with the degree-4 rule of the finite elements (exact for the product of two P2 fields). A real expression answers a number, a complex one [re, im]. `measure` is the area or volume of the region. `revolution: true` weights by 2 pi r for a body of revolution (a 2D r-z mesh). BATCH REDUCTIONS: pass `solutions` (`"all"` or a list of 0-based indices), `by_region: true`, or a batch `expr` list `["abs2(Ex)", "abs2(Ey)"]` / named map `{"energy": "...", "ex2": "..."}` to evaluate every `(solution, region, expr)` combination in a single bit-exact quadrature pass. Answers `stale` and `age_s` of what it read. FORMULAS (every `expr` of the reductions takes one): a text such as `abs(Ex)^2 * eps_r` or `where(x > 0, T, 0)`, parsed once and evaluated at each point in Rust. Numbers (`2j` is imaginary), `pi`, `e`, `+ - * / ^`, comparisons, `and or not`; functions `abs abs2 re im conj sqrt exp sin cos arg log log10 tan sinh cosh tanh atan step min max atan2` and `where(cond, a, b)` (only the branch that applies is evaluated, so `where(x != 0, 1/x, 0)` is safe). Names: the coordinates `x y z`; the fields of the result (`Ex`, `T`; in backticks when the name is not an identifier, `` `|E|` ``; `` `ems:Ex` `` or `` `ems:1:Ex` `` in backticks for another physics or solution); material values by their descriptor name (`eps_r`, `rho`; `eps` means `eps_r`; `material("rho")` to be explicit); `region("Si")` is 1 inside the region and 0 outside. A name like `E` stands for the vector (Ex, Ey, Ez) when the solution has those components: `dot(a, b)`, `inner(a, b)` (conjugates a), `cross`, `norm(v)`, `norm2(v)`, `E.x`. Orders, comparisons, `log` and `tan` read real values: wrap a complex one in `abs`, `re` or `im`. A material value is the one the solver saw in each cell. A tensor property (`eps_r`, `k`, `alpha`) has its entries as `eps_r_xx`, `eps_r_yy`, `eps_r_zz`, `eps_r_xy`, `eps_r_xz`, `eps_r_yz` in wafer axes with the crystal orientation applied (an isotropic material is the scalar times the identity); the plain `eps_r` is refused on a mesh where some material is a tensor. BOUNDARY INTEGRALS: with `boundary` (an outer boundary such as "window.top", an interface "oxide|silicon", or an interior 3D sheet) the sum is over the facets of the boundary instead of the cells: a line integral on a 2D mesh, a surface integral on a 3D one, with `revolution` weighting by 2 pi r. The formula may use `nx`, `ny`, `nz`, the unit normal in wafer axes, so the flux of a vector F is `dot(F, [nx, ny, nz])`. At an interface or interior sheet give `side` (a region name, or "+z"/"-z" for a sheet inside one region); the normal points out of it. On an outer boundary no `side` is needed. `wavelength` (m) reads the material values at that wavelength, not the study's; the fields stay those of the solve.
